title: [review] project-LICHEN-worker6-fcs3: protect_response(include_piv=false) bypasses request_kid validation and allow_no_piv_response guard
description:
The commit replaced calls through TestProtect::protect_response_with_piv (which went through reserve_sender -> protect_response_with_reserved_piv with proper request_kid != self.recipient_id() checks) with direct calls to Context::protect_response(include_piv=false). The direct path:
1. Does NOT validate request_kid matches recipient_id
2. Does NOT check allow_no_piv_response flag
This causes 10 test failures and is a correctness regression.

Failing tests:
- restored_context_rejects_response_without_piv
- supplied_material_restores_authoritative_state_and_disables_no_piv
- fresh_context_activates_only_after_atomic_registration
- response_without_piv_requires_requester_identity
- response_without_piv_is_one_shot_per_request
- oversized_explicit_piv_response_does_not_poison_valid_retry
- delayed_explicit_piv_ordinary_response_ignores_peer_replay_window
- dropped_pending_response_preserves_committed_window_across_large_jump
- public_unprotect_rejects_malformed_inner_options
- test_roundtrip_with_0xff_in_class_e_options

Fix: protect_response(include_piv=false) must validate request_kid == recipient_id() and check allow_no_piv_response before proceeding.
